newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Kodak confident about Japanese film dispute.
newsitem.headline: Kodak confident about Japanese film dispute.

text.p: The chairman and chief executive officer of Eastman Kodak Co said on Tuesday the U.S. has a strong case in accusing Tokyo of thwarting competition in its photographic film and paper market.
"I feel good about it," George Fisher of Kodak told Reuters in an interview, adding "it looks very strong and the U.S. government obviously did a lot of work on extracting the facts."

U.S. trade officials filed last week a 200-page complaint with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) against Japan, saying its liberalisation countermeasures were aimed at shielding domestic market leaders from foreign competition.
Fisher declined to comment on claims by the lawyers of Japan's Fuji Photo Film Co Ltd that the U.S. arguments were groundless.

"All of those things are government actions which the WTO has jurisdiction over. This is really a question of law," he said. "This is a historic case. This will impact many industries other than photographic which makes it so significant."

The WTO is not expected to reach a decision on the dispute until October. Fisher was in Singapore for a meeting of the international advisory council of Singapore's Economic Development Board. -- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
